draft_persistence.chosen: B — ModelDraft as a database entity
draft_persistence.rationale: A training container has no browser: it authenticates with a run token hashed into a row, reads its spec from /claim, and writes logs and metrics back over HTTP. A client-only jotai draft (MODEL-FLOW-002 as built) is unreachable from that process, so training could not run against it at all. Mirrors DatasetDraft (DS-LAKE-005), which solved the identical problem for the dataset wizard and is already proven in production — including the abandon-not-delete rule and the adopt-by-pointer save.

rejected.A — nullable modelId on ModelTrainingRun: Would work, but leaves the draft's own configuration (name, location, dataset, algorithm, target, split) with nowhere server-side to live, so Step 4's Save Model would still have to trust a client-supplied config. DatasetDraft exists precisely to avoid that.
rejected.C — create Model at training, flip statu: Directly contradicts the global definition of done. Also leaks: an abandoned wizard leaves a Model row in the workspace listing.

persistence_boundary_clarified.note: 'No database commit before Save Model' means no persistent MODEL record. It does not mean no writes at all. ModelDraft, ModelTrainingRun, ModelTrainingRunLog and ModelFineTuningJob are all written before Save Model — they are job and workspace rows, the same class of row PreprocessingJob and DatasetArtifact occupy during the dataset wizard, where DS-LAKE-005 already accepted them. What Save Model creates is the Model itself, and it adopts everything else by pointer.

artifact_scope.note: Run outputs are written under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/, not models/{modelId}/runs/{runId}/ — a modelId does not exist when the container uploads. Save Model adopts those objects by pointer (never copies bytes), the same rule DatasetArtifact.datasetId's own schema comment states. is_model_run_key/model_run_key must accept the draft scope; see MODEL-FLOW-006-T07.

fine_tuning_undefined.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-25, user decision. This ledger's own guess above turned out right: 'fine-tuning' = a hyperparameter search — one algorithm, one artifact, one train/test split, N hyperparameter sets tried in sequence, best kept by RMSE (not R² — see MODEL-FLOW-005's own implementation note for why). Not fine-tuning in the transfer-learning sense, and not a retrain on different/widened data — that reading was explicitly considered and rejected. MODEL-FLOW-005 built 2026-08-25 on this definition; T01-T08 there are no longer speculative. MODEL-SERVE-004 (/retrain) is the SAME question under decisions.retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question and is NOT auto-unblocked by this note — whoever picks it up applies this same answer there and updates that ledger's own decision, not this one.

serving_is_a_separate_ledger.rationale: This file's project is 'Model Creation Flow Refactor' and its global_definition_of_done is written entirely in terms of the five-step wizard and the Save Model persistence boundary. Serving is downstream of that boundary, has a different lifecycle (a long-running service, not a job that exits), a different failure model, and a different audience. Folding it in would move progress from 3/10 to 3/16 with no work regressing, and would leave MODEL-FLOW-008's end-to-end criterion looking incomplete for reasons unrelated to the flow it verifies. Same precedent this ledger already set twice: MODEL-FLOW-011 was kept out of MODEL-FLOW-002 for the same reason, and DS-LAKE put the DatasetDraft entity and its sweeper nine features apart.
serving_is_a_separate_ledger.coupling: Four hooks remain in THIS file and are added below: MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 (record what serving needs at adoption time), MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 (do not delete an adopted prefix), the note on MODEL-FLOW-005 that /retrain is the SAME undefined operation, and one new global_definition_of_done line. Everything else lives in MODEL-SERVE.

retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question.note: A serving-plane POST /retrain and MODEL-FLOW-005's Fine-Tuning are not two features that happen to be similar — they are the same unanswered question wearing two names, and answering it once answers both. decisions.fine_tuning_undefined already states why: train.py fits once and exits, and HistGradientBoostingRegressor has no incremental warm start. Whatever /retrain turns out to mean (a fresh fit on a widened window, a hyperparameter search reusing the split, or a genuine warm start on a framework that supports one) is the same thing MODEL-FLOW-005 is blocked on. MODEL-SERVE-004 is therefore recorded as blocked on the identical decision rather than as independent work, so that resolving it cannot be double-counted.

serving_artifacts_stay_under_the_draft_p.note: MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 adopts run artifacts BY POINTER and never copies bytes, which is correct and matches DatasetArtifact. The consequence for serving, which nothing in this file states yet: the object a production model loads lives at drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/, permanently, under a prefix whose name says 'draft'. That is acceptable — renaming it would mean copying bytes, which the adoption rule exists to avoid — but it makes MODEL-FLOW-011-T02 (reclaim the runs' object prefixes) capable of deleting the bytes a live model is serving. See MODEL-FLOW-011-T05.

bucket_layout_is_downstream.note: MODEL-SERVE-007 separates object storage into buckets by retention class. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR THIS LEDGER, neither reopening a completed task. (1) MODEL-FLOW-003-T08's key shapes are UNCHANGED — every guard it built is key-structural and bucket-blind, confirmed by MODEL-FLOW-004's live execution of is_committed_artifact_key, so drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/ keeps its exact string in whichever bucket holds it. Nothing to redo. (2) MODEL-FLOW-011-T02's prefix reclaim will run against a bucket, so it must resolve the bucket rather than assume one; and once `models` is its own bucket, T05's run-level guard is additionally expressible as a bucket-scoped rule an operator can see — which is strictly better than a predicate only this repo knows about. Recorded here so whoever picks up 011 does not hardcode `datasets` into a sweep.

tasks.title: Record the target in feature_spec.json so the leakage guard can fire
tasks.detail: train.py::assert_no_target_leakage reads derived_from_target, target_y and target_scaled from feature_spec.json. build_feature_spec(features, selected_columns, scalers) has no target parameter and emits none of the three, so `derived` is always empty and the guard returns before checking anything. This is the highest-severity item in the plan: the failure it catches LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS. A lab target sampled daily against a 1-minute PI grid with any target-derived lag feature yields R² near 1.0, and Step 3 would render that with a convincing actual-vs-predicted chart. Requires threading the target through FeaturesRequest -> the NestJS DTO -> the client's Step 4 call, and computing derived_from_target from the feature configs. target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target must NOT enter featureHash: they describe how a run READS the artifact, not how it was built, so two runs with different targets against the same bytes must still share a hash.
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18. build_feature_spec gained an optional 4th target_y param; when set it adds target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target AFTER the hash is computed (never entering it). derived_from_target is a TRANSITIVE closure (a forward pass tracking every column that reads the target or an already-tainted column), not a direct-read check — the original task text under-specified this, and a direct-read predicate would miss a feature chained off an earlier target-derived feature. artifact_service.py::features() now also calls the existing (previously orphaned) force_keep_target helper once and reuses that same effective column list for both select_columns and build_feature_spec, so the spec never claims a different column set than what was actually written. Threaded through CreateFeaturesSchema (NestJS), both python call sites (inline /features route and the async job path incl. readFeatureRecipe), and the client (dwTargetTagAtom -> useDatasetGoldWarm -> startFeaturesJob), with targetTag added to the warming effect's dependency list. assert_target_is_unscaled was deliberately left uncalled — a scaled target is recorded truthfully and blocked later at training time by train.py's existing check, not at dataset-save time. Verified via 6 new pytest cases in test_feature_spec_quirks.py (14/14 pass) proving build_feature_spec's own contract, PLUS a 7th seam test (test_features_force_keeps_target_through_select_columns in test_artifact_service_features.py) proving the wiring at the call site actually works: with selected_columns deliberately omitting the target, both the WRITTEN BYTES and the spec's selectedColumns retain it — the first-pass draft of this note cited only the unit-level tests, which would have missed a broken call site. Full apps/python suite: 617 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (test_features_writes_feature_spec_sidecar_and_returns_its_key, confirmed via git stash to predate this branch), 66 skipped.

features.implementation:
Done 2026-08-25. AUDITED FIRST, per CLAUDE.md §18: this entry was one of the thin, never-re-audited ones (5 bare task titles, no detail) — read against the tree before scoping, not against the prior task titles. FINDING: Phase3Evaluation was not 'using a stale API', it used NO real data source at all — it re-materialised the dataset client-side and fit a 2-variable OLS line over the target plus 'the first non-target tag it finds' (`computeFit`, old `lib/model-metrics.ts:150`), ignoring the trained algorithm entirely. The run's real output was already captured on SUCCEEDED (MODEL-FLOW-003-T05/T06) into `mpTrainingResultAtom`/`mpArtifactRefAtom` and READ BY NOTHING — confirmed by grep, zero readers of either atom before this pass.

No read path for a run's predictions existed anywhere in the stack — confirmed by executing the guard live: `is_committed_artifact_key('drafts/{d}/runs/{r}/predictions.parquet')` returns False, and the four existing parse endpoints (`/rows`, `/preview`, `/histogram`, `/scatter`) all route through `sample_rows`, which assumes per-tag `__status` sidecar columns a run's 3-column `{timestamp, y_true, y_pred}` frame does not have. Built new: `POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/predictions` (`artifact_service.run_predictions`) — reads the full test-split frame, computes `row_count`/`residual_sd`/a `residual_rmse_check` cross-check/y-ranges over the FULL frame (no decimation branch: `MAX_PREDICTION_POINTS=20000`, comfortably above the largest observed run at 4,633 rows; a run over the cap is refused by name rather than silently sampled — deferred design recorded in `schemas/preprocess.py`'s own comment for whoever hits it first), and optionally reads `run_manifest.json` for `derived_from_target`/`target_scaled`. `GET .../model-drafts/:draftId/runs/:runId/predictions` (`getDraftRunPredictionsService`) resolves `predictionsKey`/`manifestKey` OFF THE RUN ROW, never from the request — same discipline `mintUploadUrls` already applies on the write side — and refuses (404, naming which) a run that has not SUCCEEDED or has no `predictionsKey`. Client: `modelDraftRunService.predictions` + new `useDraftRunEvaluation` hook, keyed on `(draftId, runId)` with a fallback to `ModelDraft.currentRunId` when the atom hint is empty (mirrors `use-model-training.ts`'s own reconnect-effect trust in that field). `lib/model-metrics.ts` rewritten: `computeFit`/`computeMetrics`/`pickDefaultPair` DELETED (grepped: Step 4 was `computeFit`'s only caller; the other two already had zero callers, confirmed dead before removal), replaced by `fitFromRun(points, {r2,rmse,sd})` — a pure wrap, no fitting. `phase-3-evaluation.tsx` rewritten around the hook; kept `METRIC_KEY`/`METRIC_META`/`buildFitRows`/both chart components/the histogram+Q-Q section entirely unchanged, per the seam the old module's own doc comment specified.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO A PRIOR READING, RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED (MinIO screenshot findings in MODEL-FLOW-010/MODEL-SERVE-000 called `holdoutMetrics` null on every observed run and left the cause open): (1) confirmed via the one real log line that exists (`Holdout replay skipped: Could not read '.../validate_data.parquet': NoSuchKey`) — it fails at the REPLAY step on a missing source object, not at presign. `train.py`'s own comment already documents this as the common case (no holdout on the dataset), not a bug. (2) There IS a real, separate, still-latent defect one line later: `tryReplayHoldout`'s own `presignArtifact({source_key: targetKey})` call presigns `.../validate_ready.parquet`, which the SAME committed-artifact guard refuses (verified by executing it: `is_committed_artifact_key` returns False for that key too) — it has simply never been reached by any observed run. Recorded against DS-LAKE-018-T05, not fixed here — it is not this ledger's to fix, and 'holdoutMetrics is null' already has its real, boring cause.

SCOPE DECISIONS (user-confirmed, not unilateral): (a) the 'Compare with…' control is DISABLED with a stated reason, not removed and not left fabricating a series — `seededNoise`/`comparePoints`/`compareFit` deleted; no saved Model can supply a real predicted series until MODEL-FLOW-007 adopts a run by pointer, so faking one here would be the same defect this feature exists to remove. (b) Resuming a TRAINED draft into Step 4 (MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's recorded gap 1) stays OUT of scope — `useDraftRunEvaluation`'s `(draftId, runId)` key with the `currentRunId` fallback is deliberately shaped so that resume work is a follow-on, not a rewrite, when someone picks it up. (c) Metric cards stay exactly r2/rmse/sd — MAE rides in the served payload, undisplayed, rather than widening `MetricKey` against acceptance criterion 1.

HONEST EMPTY STATES ADDED — the one place criterion 1 ('UI remains unchanged') had to bend, stated rather than discovered: no run yet, run still training, run FAILED/CANCELED (names the reason), and the load/error states from the hook itself. Load-bearing among these: `use-model-wizard-mode.ts:169-170` force-unlocks all 5 steps and sets `trainState:'done'` on EDIT MODE purely because the dataset resolved — there is no run, no `runId`, and `useModelCommit` persists neither on Save. Step 4 in edit mode therefore always hits the no-run empty state until MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 records a run reference on the saved Model.

Renamed 'Validation residual diagnostics' -> 'Test-split residual diagnostics': `predictions.parquet` is the run's TEST split, not the validation holdout, which is a distinct object with its own (currently always-null, see above) metrics shown on Step 2's own Holdout panel — the old heading misnamed what the histogram/Q-Q actually summarise.

Built 2026-08-25, backend only — no client wiring in this pass (not asked for; the wizard's existing AutoML/Find-Best-Params toggles stay disabled, MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's own note still applies). No new spawn/claim/complete/queue infrastructure: a fine-tuning job is a ModelFineTuningJob row that GROUPS ordinary ModelTrainingRun rows (new nullable fineTuningJobId FK), each one launched through the EXACT MODEL-FLOW-003 machinery, live-verified end to end. This is the direct build-out of MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's own blocked_reason: 'AutoML is N runs orchestrated ABOVE the container ... not a flag passed into train.py.'

Extraction, not duplication: `ModelRunLaunchAuthorizedService.createDraftRunService` was split into `assertDraftWritable` (access+lifecycle gate, now public) + `launchDraftRun` (the actual write, now takes an optional `fineTuningJobId`, no user/role param). `createDraftRunService` itself is unchanged in behaviour — it calls both in sequence — verified by its own pre-existing 7-test suite passing unmodified. `launchDraftRun` is what both the job's first run (`ModelFineTuningAuthorizedService.createJob`) and every chained run (`advanceJobForRun`) call — a fine-tuning child run goes through the SAME buildRunData validation, the SAME transaction shape, the SAME trackSpawn fire-and-forget spawn as a normal single run.

Advancing a job (`advanceJobForRun`) is IDEMPOTENT, keyed by a compare-and-swap `updateMany` WHERE `(id, currentRunId, status IN (QUEUED,RUNNING))` — calling it twice for the same terminated run is a no-op the second time, unit-tested directly. Two call sites, both wired: `ModelRunAuthorizedService.complete()` calls it as a best-effort nudge (wrapped so it can NEVER fail the container's webhook response — a training container has no way to retry a 500), and `getJobService` calls it opportunistically on every read, so a job whose nudge was lost (the exact class of gap MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 already tracks for a single orphaned run) still advances the next time anyone looks at it. No cron, no queue, no BullMQ/Redis — CLAUDE.md §11's instruction to reuse or justify before introducing one.

REAL BUG CAUGHT WHILE WIRING, not by review: `complete()`'s existing SUCCEEDED-draft branch unconditionally set `ModelDraft.currentRunId = runId` — correct for a normal run, WRONG for a fine-tuning child run finishing mid-search, which would have pointed the draft at whichever INTERMEDIATE hyperparameter set happened to finish, not the eventual winner (and MODEL-FLOW-004's `useDraftRunEvaluation` would have shown that intermediate run in Step 4 for the whole search's duration). Fixed by excluding `!!run.fineTuningJobId` from that branch — only `advanceJobForRun`'s own completion branch may now set `ModelDraft.currentRunId`, and only to the true best run. Live-verified this fix works: `bestRunId` was correctly `86728c46...` (rmse 0.659) not `f8c1c1e0...` (the run that finished LAST, rmse 0.677, worse) — see V01's note.

Selection metric is RMSE, minimized, not configurable — R² was explicitly rejected: a real observed run scored r2 = -1,110,858 (MODEL-FLOW-004's own finding) while rmse stayed a sane, comparable number. Concurrency: a partial unique index (`ModelFineTuningJob_one_live_per_draft`, hand-added to the migration same precedent as 20260818021900_model_flow_002_owner_check) refuses a second QUEUED/RUNNING job per draft at the database — live-verified with a real concurrent-POST 409, not just a service-level check.

tasks.title: Support Fine-Tuning retry
tasks.verification_note: Only a FAILED job retries, relaunching the EXACT hyperparameter set that failed (`completedRuns` deliberately not incremented on failure, so `sets[completedRuns]` is always that set) and resuming the sequence from there. Live-verified against a real (deliberately-triggered) FAILED job: relaunch succeeded, job returned to RUNNING with a fresh currentRunId. NOT covered, stated explicitly: a job stuck RUNNING because its current run is itself orphaned (a nest --watch restart killing the in-memory container tracker mid-flight, MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's own observed incident) — retry only fires on FAILED; that gap is MODEL-FLOW-011-T04's, not duplicated here.

features.title: Persist Model Configuration and Artifacts Before Final Save
features.description: Store model configuration, training configuration, evaluation results, and model artifacts in temporary or external storage while keeping the final Model database record uncommitted.
features.implementation:
AUDITED FIRST 2026-08-25, per CLAUDE.md §18 — another thin, never-re-audited entry (6 bare task titles). FIVE OF SIX TASKS WERE ALREADY SATISFIED by work already landed: training config lives on ModelDraft (8 PATCHable fields) + the authoritative reproducible spec on ModelTrainingRun (checksum, imageDigest, featureSpecKey, seed, computed cut_timestamp — strictly more than the draft holds); fine-tuning config on ModelFineTuningJob (built in -005, same session); evaluation on ModelTrainingRun.metrics/.holdoutMetrics (read path built in -004); artifact references are the run's own modelKey/metricsKey/manifestKey/predictionsKey; 'latest valid' is ModelDraft.currentRunId (+ ModelFineTuningJob.bestRunId). This is architecturally the SAME shape the ledger's own precedent already uses for datasets: DatasetDraft holds identity + currentArtifactId, the recipe lives on DatasetArtifact.operations — ModelDraft holds identity + currentRunId, the spec lives on the run row.

THE ONE REAL DEFECT, found by querying the live dev DB rather than reading code alone: `ModelConfigSchema` (model.authorized.dto.ts) was `.passthrough()` and declared only 6 of the ~18 keys the client actually sends, with its own comment stating 'the canonical shape lives in the client type; the backend only stores it round-trip.' A live audit of all 16 existing Model rows found the drift that allowed: 6 dead pre-Data-Studio ETL keys (dataSource, fillStrategies, timeRange, selectedTags, customDateRange, savedSourceId) persisted verbatim, and BOTH targetVariable (declared, singular) and targetVariables (used, undeclared, plural) present across rows — the field real data mostly uses survived only because nothing validated it. Also found: trainTestSplit is a PERCENTAGE in Model.data.config (70/80/85 observed) but a FRACTION on ModelDraft.splitRatio and ModelTrainingRun.splitSpec.ratio — three homes, two units, unvalidated on the one that matters here.

FIXED: ModelConfigSchema rewritten from .passthrough() to .strict(), declaring every field actually seen in production — live fields typed properly (targetVariables[], algorithms[], findBestModel/findBestParams, lossFunction, deployment, etc.), the 6 dead ETL keys and the singular targetVariable kept as explicitly @deprecated z.unknown()/string fields so legacy rows keep validating. trainTestSplit validated as a percentage (.min(50).max(95)) with a comment naming all three homes and their units — unifying the unit is -007's job, when Save Model can derive it from the adopted run's own splitSpec instead of trusting the browser. New DeploymentConfigSchema declared (autoRetrain/warnSd/criticalSd/driftMonitor/driftThresholdPct) even though 0 of 16 rows carry it and no UI currently writes it (phase-4-deploy.tsx's own docblock says so) — -007 decides whether to wire the UI or delete the field and its 5 client atoms, not decided here.

THE TRAP THIS DESIGN HAD TO AVOID, LIVE-VERIFIED CLOSED: updateModelService replaces config WHOLESALE, not by merge, and edit mode loads an existing Model's config then sends it back on save — a naively strict schema would have broken every edit of the 16 legacy rows. Verified against a REAL legacy row (5848c20f-..., carrying all 6 dead ETL keys) through the RUNNING backend: PATCH with its own config re-sent returned 200, and a direct DB equality check (`data->'config' = <original>::jsonb`) confirmed the stored blob is byte-identical, not merely 'still valid'. The refusal half was verified the same way: PATCHing an unknown key against the same live row returned 400 naming the exact key.

Also tightened: PatchModelDraftSchema.hyperparameters (model-draft.authorized.dto.ts) went from z.unknown() to the same HyperparametersSchema scalar constraint the run path already enforces — a draft could otherwise hold a hyperparameter value CreateTrainingRunSchema would refuse at Start Training, discovered only then. Confirmed compatible with the client's own HyperparamValue type (string|number|boolean|null) before tightening.

STILL RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE (handed to -007, which is where they actually belong): 0 of 18 training runs have ever had modelId set; 0 of 24 drafts have ever had savedModelId set — the draft-to-Model bridge has never been exercised, confirming -007-T11's own 'UNVERIFIED PREMISE' framing was right to doubt itself. Save Model's commit payload (use-model-commit.ts:56-68) sends no runId/modelKey/metrics at all — this is why a saved Model today cannot be traced to what produced it, and it is exactly what -007-T10's adopt-by-pointer is for. Also recorded for whoever next touches these areas: two dead client inconsistencies (lossFunction default disagrees between resetWizardAtom 'mse' and resetPipeline 'rmse'; resetPipeline hardcodes the metric array instead of importing METRIC_KEYS), ~29 dead client atoms/hooks from the pre-Data-Studio wizard, and CreateModelRunSchema (model-run.authorized.dto.ts) confirmed dead code via grep with a harmless bound mismatch against the live schema.

features.title: Sequence Model Training (LSTM/GRU) — Deferred, Needs a Windowing Pipeline
features.blocked_on: lstm/gru need a data-SHAPE change (2D samples x features -> 3D samples x timesteps x features) upstream of the split, plus a sequence_length hyperparameter and a deep-learning runtime this image doesn't carry. This is not a build_model branch — recorded separately per CLAUDE.md 17 (missing infrastructure, unclear contract) rather than left as an omission when MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's catalogue half was resolved (images/trainer/train.py; apps/client/store/model-pipeline.ts Algorithm catalogue).
features.description: The wizard's Algorithm catalogue includes lstm and gru; train.py's build_model raises a named error for both rather than the generic 'Unsupported algorithm' message, and the wizard disables both inline (AlgorithmSelector) so a user cannot select a run that will always fail. This feature is what it would take to actually run them — not scoped or estimated as part of the 10-algorithm tabular extension, because the shape of the work is different in kind, not degree.

tasks.title: Design the windowing step (2D -> 3D) and where it runs in the pipeline
tasks.detail: Sequence models need (samples, timesteps, features); train.py currently builds a flat (samples, features) frame and hands feature_cols straight to fit(). Windowing must happen BEFORE chronological_split (train.py:143-164) — windowing after the split lets a window's timesteps span the train/test boundary, which is exactly the ordering bug the module docstring already warns about for the non-Good-target drop (train.py:8-12), just one step later in the pipeline.

tasks.title: Extend the leakage guard to cover window-straddling, not just row-wise lags
tasks.detail: assert_no_target_leakage (train.py:101-140) reasons about row-wise lag features via the target's labelled-vs-row median sampling gap — it says nothing about a WINDOW that starts before the cut and ends after it. A window straddling chronological_split's boundary is a leakage path today's guard cannot see, because it was written for a different failure shape (a lag column repeating the current target value, not a window spanning two sides of a split). This needs its own check, not a parameter on the existing one.

tasks.title: Add sequence_length (and validate epochs/batch_size/hidden_size against it) to the hyperparameter contract
tasks.detail: Correction to an earlier framing of this gap: HYPERPARAMS.lstm / HYPERPARAMS.gru (apps/client/lib/training-config.ts:212-264) already collect epochs, batch_size, and hidden_size — those are NOT missing. The one genuinely missing field is sequence_length, the value that actually defines the window this feature needs. Both the DTO's HyperparametersSchema and the client catalogue need it added, and epochs/batch_size need a documented default now that they will actually be consumed by a real fit loop instead of sitting unused.

tasks.title: Add a deep-learning runtime to the trainer image and re-audit sizing
tasks.detail: Needs tensorflow or torch (+~1.5-2 GB), which changes build time and the memory/tmpfs sizing MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 already audited and closed (8 GiB Memory, no swap; 2 GiB tmpfs /scratch sharing the same cgroup — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts). That audit's 'not a defect to fix' conclusion was reached against the current sklearn-only image; it does not automatically extend to an image carrying a full DL framework and this needs its own pass, not an inherited one.

features.description: A review step between Model Setup and Training Configuration. Shows which data source the selected dataset came from, its per-tag statistics, the same DataAnalysisCard the dataset wizard's Step 3.1 uses, and the held-out validation window — so an engineer sees WHAT they are about to train on before configuring HOW. Includes a route back into the dataset wizard for a dataset that needs changing.
userDecisions: STEP COUNT (resolved): five steps. The flow becomes Setup -> Dataset Review -> Training Configuration -> Evaluation -> Save Model. This file's global_definition_of_done currently asserts four steps in four separate lines and MODEL-FLOW-008 verifies by step number; all of them are rewritten as part of T01 rather than left to contradict the feature that renumbered them.

EDIT DATASET RE-ENTRY (resolved): warn-and-navigate, NOT an overlay and NOT a full URL-addressable resume. An overlay would keep the model wizard mounted and make Back a close rather than a rehydration — genuinely smaller than a resume mechanism — but it rests on three unverified assumptions about the dataset wizard (mountable outside its route, no atom collision, no reset-on-mount). Three unknowns for one button is a poor trade against an honest dialog. The draft is PATCHed current before navigating and is resumable from the models list (T08).
findings: RESTORED 2026-08-25. This array was found holding six MODEL-SERVE findings (run_manifest.json / serving bundle / artifact pinning / one bucket / MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 / checksum sidecar) — verbatim duplicates of MODEL-SERVE.findings, and this feature's own five findings were gone. Six pointers in this same feature (T05, T07's detail AND its note, V02, and acceptance criteria 3 and 5) resolve to them, so every one of those was reading a finding about serving. The serving findings live in MODEL-SERVE and are removed here. The originals are restored below from what those six pointers assert about them; wording is reconstructed, the claims are not.

DATAANALYSISCARD WAS DRAFT-SCOPED, THEN MADE STORE-AGNOSTIC (two reversals, both kept visible). Originally judged 'reusable but type-gated' — wrong on three counts: it read dwDraftIdAtom/dwDraftArtifactIdAtom/dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom directly; its histogram/boxplot/scatter tabs hit DRAFT-scoped routes with no datasetId-scoped twin (only correlation had one); and it rendered FeatureTransformDialog, a write to dwScalerConfigsAtom, inside a step that configures nothing. RESOLVED 2026-08-20: compose instead of reuse. REVERSED 2026-08-21 on explicit user request: the card is mounted after all, but only after all three defects were fixed at source — optional datasetId/artifactId props short-circuit the dw* routing, showTransforms={false} suppresses the dialog and stops it inheriting dwScalerConfigsAtom. What remains shared is dwHiddenTagsAtom/dwFocusedTagAtom via useDatasetTagSelection — view state, accepted knowingly. Dropped in unmodified, four of six tabs would have shown 'pending' forever.

THE STEP HOLDS NO SERVER STATE OF ITS OWN. It reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing. ModelDraft needs no new column and receives no PATCH from this step — stated up front so it is not given one by reflex. (T07 later carved out ONE exception, the user-confirmed Edit Dataset flush; see acceptance criterion 3.)

EDITING A DATASET DOES NOT REMOVE IT. The Dataset row keeps its id; what changes is currentArtifactId, and possibly the tag list. So datasetId on the ModelDraft stays valid across an edit and must NOT be cleared. What genuinely goes stale is the selected TARGET, if the edit dropped that tag — a different field with a different consequence.

RESUME IS THE ONLY RETURN PATH THAT PRESERVES ANYTHING (T07/T08). Browser Back re-mounts the wizard with no ?draftId=, and useModelWizardMode's create branch calls reset() unconditionally — so Back wipes the jotai atoms even though the server row survives. That is why the hand-off dialog says so outright, and why reconciliation lives in the resume branch rather than a general on-return hook: there is no other return.

tasks.title: Validation-holdout panel
tasks.detail:
CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-08-20: checked against the code and the holdout's missing/Bad rate exists NOWHERE — not on DatasetArtifact, not in ArtifactStatsSchema/ArtifactStats, not computed anywhere in artifact_service.py. The holdout window itself also has no client-facing read path: it lives on the BRONZE sibling of the run's GOLD/FINAL artifact, resolved by runId — the same lookup tryReplayHoldout (model-run.authorized.service.ts) already does server-side, never exposed to a browser. This is a real build, not a composition of existing reads:

1. Python — artifact_service.py's materialize() holdout branch and resplit_holdout() both already hold validate_frame in memory; pass missing_pct(validate_frame) (object_store.py) into _stats_payload as a new validation_missing_pct field. ArtifactStatsResponse (schemas/preprocess.py) gains the field, nullable/optional like validation_row_count beside it.
2. Prisma — DatasetArtifact.validationMissingPct Float?, migrated.
3. Backend — ArtifactStatsSchema (dataset-version.authorized.dto.ts) gains validation_missing_pct; persisted in both places that already set validationRowCount (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts).
4. New read endpoint GET /datasets/:id/artifacts/:artifactId/holdout: resolve the artifact's runId, find its BRONZE sibling, and if validationRowCount is set return {holdoutFrom, holdoutTo, rowCount, missingPct} — window bounds from Python /metadata against validateDataKey (footer-only, bounded), missingPct from the new column.

THE MISSING RATE IS NOT OPTIONAL for any holdout captured going forward. A holdout written before this change returns missingPct: null, and the panel says so plainly ('missing rate not recorded for this holdout') rather than omitting the field silently or inventing a compute-on-read scan (which would defeat the bounded-read discipline V03 checks). DS-LAKE-018's resolved no-imputation decision means the holdout stays raw, so a MISSING_VALUE hole reaches predict() and depresses the score with no trace of why; its own T05 already requires the rate be published beside every metric for that reason.

tasks.title: Edit Dataset hand-off — warn, persist, reconcile
tasks.detail:
DEFERRED 2026-08-20: out of scope for the T01-T06 pass (composition of the review step itself). Explicitly NOT started because its own dialog-copy rule below is coupled to T08 shipping, and T08 has not. When picked up: PATCH the draft to current BEFORE navigating. useModelDraftSync's PATCH is 600ms-debounced, so a click landing inside that window leaves the server row stale; ensureDraftId already exists for this class of 'the server must know before we do something irreversible' problem.

DO NOT clear datasetId — see findings. Clearing it would discard a reference that stayed valid and force the user to re-pick something that never changed.

RECONCILE ON RETURN, by whatever path: re-fetch the dataset, invalidate every artifact-keyed hook, and CHECK THE TARGET STILL EXISTS in the new artifact's tag list. A dropped target surviving in mpTargetVariableAtom fails at run creation with a pyarrow 'No match for FieldRef.Name' error that names a column and explains nothing — the same class of failure the Step 3.1 correlation tab already hit once.

DIALOG COPY MUST MATCH WHAT SHIPS: it may claim the draft is saved and resumable only if T08 ships. If T08 is cut, the copy says the configuration is discarded. A dialog promising a resume nothing can honour is worse than one admitting the loss.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-21. The Edit Dataset button + AlertDialog live in phase-2-dataset-review.tsx, but the flush-then-navigate ORDER — the only part that can be got wrong invisibly — lives in hooks/model/use-dataset-edit-handoff.ts, so it is testable and the step stays a composition shell.

useModelDraftSync gained `{ autoSync }` (default true, so phase-2-training-config is untouched) and `flush()`. One shared `syncNow` writer now backs both the debounced effect and the explicit flush; flush cancels the armed 600ms debounce first (leaving it armed would re-send the same body after the user has already navigated) and, unlike the effect, it THROWS — so a failed PATCH aborts the navigation, keeps the user on the step and surfaces a toast. The review step passes autoSync:false, so finding #3 still holds exactly as written for mount and for every control in the step; acceptance criterion 3 was REWORDED to carve out the user-confirmed hand-off rather than left asserting something the code no longer does.

datasetId is NOT cleared, per the findings. The seed-and-navigate itself was extracted out of useDataStudio.handleDatasetEdit into hooks/dataset/use-dataset-edit-navigation.ts and both callers now share one implementation — that indirection is also what keeps V02's store/dataset-studio ban intact, since the hand-off needs initDatasetWizardForEditAtom and the step itself still imports no dw* atom.

RECONCILE-ON-RETURN landed in the resume path (T08), which is the only return path that preserves anything: browser Back re-mounts useModelWizardMode with no draftId and hits its reset(). Resume re-fetches the dataset, and that re-fetch IS the artifact-hook invalidation — useArtifactMetadata / useArtifactColumnStats / useArtifactRows / useArtifactHoldout are each keyed on (datasetId, artifactId), and the metadata module cache keys `${ownerId}:${artifactId}`, so a currentArtifactId moved by the edit is a new key in all four (checked in each file, not assumed). reconcileTarget then clears a target the edit dropped and the toast NAMES it.

DIALOG COPY MATCHES WHAT SHIPS: it claims the draft is saved and resumable, and says plainly that the browser Back button will not restore it. UPDATED 2026-08-21 with T08's relocation — it now names New Model -> Step 1 -> Drafts in progress rather than Models -> Drafts in progress, because that is where the panel actually is. A dialog pointing at a screen that no longer holds the thing it promises is the same defect as promising a resume nothing can honour.

tasks.title: Resume an ACTIVE ModelDraft from the models list
tasks.detail: DEFERRED 2026-08-20, out of scope for the T01-T06 pass. CORRECTED CLAIM: the prior detail here said 'the draft row already holds every field the wizard would restore' — checked against packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma's ModelDraft model and that is false. It has name/workspaceId/plantId/nodeId/datasetId/targetY/algorithm/hyperparameters/splitRatio/status/currentRunId — no description, no algorithms[] (multi-algorithm selection), no lossFunction, no selectedMetrics, no deploy config (autoRetrain/warnSd/criticalSd/driftMonitor/driftThresholdPct). Restore from this row is PARTIAL. The controller (model-draft.authorized.controller.ts) also has no list route yet — only POST, GET /:id, PATCH /:id, POST /:id/abandon; a GET /model-drafts?workspaceId=&status=ACTIVE is needed first. The step-position part of this task is still fine as originally scoped (derivable from status + currentRunId, no schema change) — only the 'every field' claim was wrong. When picked up, the resume dialog/toast must say what actually restores, not imply full parity.
tasks.note:
Completed 2026-08-21. Backend: GET /authorized/model-drafts, declared BEFORE @Get('/:id') because Nest matches in declaration order and a bare GET would otherwise never be reached; ListModelDraftQueryDto {workspaceId?, status?}. The owner-or-member workspace clause was extracted into a private workspaceScope(user) now shared by assertWorkspaceAccess, assertDraftAccess and the list — a second hand-written copy is how a list ends up broader than the GET it links to. An inaccessible workspaceId 404s rather than returning [] ('not yours' is a different fact from 'none here'). `status` accepts the full enum deliberately and the UI asks for ACTIVE. New spec model-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts (the module had none), 7/7 passing: scope-applied-with-no-filters, both filters, the 404, the ADMIN bypass keeping deletedAt, ISO dates + splitRatio still a FRACTION, and — because workspaceScope now backs the other three routes too — a direct comparison proving the list's WHERE.workspace is the SAME object shape assertDraftAccess builds, plus a 404 for a draft that clause filters out. Two clauses that merely agree today would pass a per-method test and diverge later.

Client: modelDraftService.list; useModelDrafts (plain local state, not useAllModels' shared-atom + module-dedup shape — one consumer, one request; a failed load hides the panel instead of erroring the page); DraftResumePanel, which renders NOTHING when there are no drafts. REVISED 2026-08-21 ON USER REQUEST: it now carries THREE ways to clear drafts as well as Resume — a per-row X, Remove selected (a checkbox per row, shown only once something is ticked), and Remove all. The remove had been withheld as MODEL-FLOW-011's, which was the wrong call for this surface — a list that only ever grows is a list people stop reading, and it sits in the wizard now, not on an admin page. It ABANDONS (POST /:id/abandon, already built): status ACTIVE -> ABANDONED, training runs untouched, so the copy says 'removed from this list', never 'deleted'. All three share ONE confirm, differing only in which drafts they hand it — three dialogs would be three copies of the same wording to keep in step — and it is confirmed rather than immediate, matching how ModelTable guards its own row-level destructive action: the X sits one mis-click from Resume, Remove all is one click from everything, and there is no undo anywhere in the UI. The dialog is held open until the server confirms, so a failed remove cannot close over rows that stayed.

No bulk endpoint was invented for this: the confirm fans out one abandon per draft and settles them all, because a bulk route that abandons some rows and fails on others has the SAME partial outcome to report — it would just hide it behind one status code. Partial failure is therefore a real state and is handled as one: all-failed keeps the dialog open and says so, some-failed closes, refetches and names the count that did not go. Selection is held by id and resolved against the current list each render, so an id whose draft has since left the list (resumed, or removed in another tab) cannot produce a 'Remove selected (1)' that removes nothing. Reclaiming the ABANDONED rows themselves is still MODEL-FLOW-011.

The list caps at 5 rows and scrolls past that (ScrollArea, fixed height): unbounded, it would push the preset picker and the dataset grid off a laptop screen, which is the opposite of what a 'pick up where you left off' affordance should do. Nothing is truncated — every draft stays reachable. The icon-only X takes an aria-label naming its draft, or a screen reader hears five identical 'remove' buttons.

RELOCATED 2026-08-21 ON USER REQUEST: the panel now sits at the TOP OF STEP 1, directly above the preset picker, not on /models/views — picking up unfinished work is a different intent from starting new, and it belongs before the choices that assume you are starting new. That move broke the mechanism, not just the placement: Resume used to push /models/create?draftId=..., which is INERT from inside the wizard (already mounted on that route, so useModelWizardMode's run-once effect never sees the changed query) — a dead button that typechecks. So the restore logic was extracted out of that effect into hooks/model/use-model-draft-resume.ts, which both entries now share: the URL keeps working on a cold mount, and Step 1 hydrates IN PLACE. Failure no longer navigates from inside the hook — the URL caller sends the user back to /models/views, the in-wizard caller leaves them where they are, because nothing was lost. Either way it is a CREATE-mode continuation, not a mode of its own, since no Model row exists yet.

Two consequences of living inside the wizard, both handled: resuming now REPLACES work the user may already have typed (impossible on the models list), so DraftResumeSection confirms first when the wizard is dirty — a name typed or a dataset chosen — and the draft already open is filtered out of its own list. New test pipeline/__tests__/draft-resume-section.test.tsx, 16/16: in-place hydrate on a clean wizard, the confirm on a dirty one, dismissal leaving it alone, the current draft not offered, nothing rendered when there are no drafts, remove confirming-then-abandoning and refetching, cancel and failure leaving the draft in place, the per-draft aria-label, the 5-row cap (no scroll container at 5, one at 6, with all 6 still reachable), Remove all abandoning every listed draft, Remove selected abandoning ONLY the ticked ones (the unticked row must survive), unticking shrinking the count, a partial failure reported rather than passed off as success, and an all-failed batch keeping the dialog open without refetching.

RESTORE IS PARTIAL AND SAYS SO, per this task's own corrected claim: the row has no description, algorithms[], lossFunction, selectedMetrics or deploy config, so the toast states exactly what came back rather than implying parity. Hydration uses RAW atom setters, never useModelPipelineNav's — every one of those calls resetTraining() and relocks highestUnlocked, and setAlgorithm additionally overwrites hyperparameters with that algorithm's defaults, which would have discarded the draft's stored set moments after restoring it. Step position: land on Step 1 so the restored choices are confirmed, unlock to 2 once the dataset resolves and NO FURTHER, because no training result is restored and an empty Evaluation step would be a lie. splitRatio fraction -> percent, and algorithm/hyperparameters are narrowed by type guard in lib/model-draft-hydration.ts rather than cast.

THREE GAPS, STATED NOT HIDDEN. (1) A TRAINED draft is reachable through the API but is not offered in the panel, because its run result is not rebuilt on resume. (2) Leaving via browser Back and starting over can leave an extra ACTIVE draft behind; reclaiming those is MODEL-FLOW-011, not this task. (3) resumeDraft does not check status: a hand-edited ?draftId= or a panel rendered before another tab saved that draft can resume a SAVED row, whose every later PATCH 409s into the debounced sync's silent catch — so the user would configure against a row that refuses updates. Narrow (the panel refetches on mount and nothing in the UI abandons a draft) and it is lifecycle territory, so it is recorded here for MODEL-FLOW-011 rather than guarded now.

acceptance_criteria: The wizard has five steps, and this file's own definition of done says five rather than still claiming four.
No existing step's behaviour changes — only its number.

The review step reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing; ModelDraft gains no column, and nothing in the step PATCHes it — not on mount, not from any control. REVISED 2026-08-21 (T07): the single exception is the Edit Dataset hand-off, which flushes the draft ONCE, after the user confirms the dialog, because criterion 8 requires the draft be persisted before leaving. That is the user walking out of the step, not the step configuring anything — enforced by passing autoSync:false to useModelDraftSync, so the debounced writer never runs here at all.
Per-tag statistics are served from the sidecar without opening data.parquet.

The review step's preview comes from a bounded server page (useArtifactRows: 200 rows x 50 tags); the step reads no dw* atom and mounts no dataset-wizard mutation UI. REVISED AGAIN 2026-08-21 (user request): the step now DOES mount DataAnalysisCard, but only after that component was made store-agnostic — it is passed an explicit datasetId/artifactId so every server-backed tab routes through the dataset-scoped artifact routes with no dw* atom deciding anything, and showTransforms={false} keeps FeatureTransformDialog (a WRITE to dwScalerConfigsAtom) out of a step that configures nothing. The 'no mutation UI' half of this criterion is therefore intact; only the 'compose instead of reuse' means of achieving it changed.
A dataset with no committed artifact shows one honest empty state, not four independent ones.
The holdout panel publishes the holdout's missing/Bad rate beside every figure it shows.
Leaving to edit a dataset persists the draft first, and the dialog states exactly what survives.
Returning after an edit re-reads the dataset and clears a target the edit removed, saying so.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft is reachable from the models list.

features.title: ModelDraft Lifecycle Reclaim
features.description: DS-LAKE-014 gave DatasetDraft a sweeper and closed the never-abandoned-ACTIVE hole for datasets. ModelDraft is a separate table with no equivalent, so the identical leak exists here: a user who closes the tab leaves an ACTIVE ModelDraft forever, because nothing calls /abandon on their behalf.
findings: DELIBERATELY NOT A TASK INSIDE MODEL-FLOW-002. That feature is completed at 100% with nine live-verified tasks; reopening it to add reclaim work would make its own completion claim false and mix verified history with unstarted work. The concerns are also independent — 002 gives the container a row to read, this decides when an unused row is released, and neither constrains the other. The DS-LAKE side already answered this question the same way: the DatasetDraft entity is DS-LAKE-005 and its sweeper is DS-LAKE-014, nine features apart.

THE STORAGE COST IS SMALLER THAN THE DATASET CASE BUT NOT ZERO. A ModelDraft owns no artifact of its own, so an abandoned one leaks a Postgres row rather than object bytes. Its ModelTrainingRuns DO write under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ (MODEL-FLOW-003-T08), and nothing reclaims those today — so the leak is real, just concentrated in the runs rather than the draft.

MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 MAKES THIS MORE FREQUENT, NOT MERELY MORE VISIBLE. Leaving the wizard to edit a dataset becomes a normal, encouraged action there; every user who does not come back leaves an ACTIVE draft behind. The leak predates that feature but its rate does not.

tasks.title: Tiered ACTIVE-draft eligibility for ModelDraft
tasks.detail: Mirror DS-LAKE-014's tiers rather than inventing a second policy: a draft owning ZERO runs releases on a short window (nothing was computed, nothing is expensive to lose); a draft owning runs releases on a long idle window (a real fit cost minutes of container time). Measure from updatedAt, the same convention DS-LAKE-014's branches use and the same one DS-LAKE-009B-T08 already had to fix once by moving OFF artifact.createdAt. A TRAINED draft is NOT eligible on either window — it holds a finished result the user may still be reviewing in Step 4, which is exactly the state Save Model consumes.

tasks.title: Reclaim the runs' object prefixes, not only the rows
tasks.detail: Abandoning a draft must also release drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ for each of its runs — otherwise the row disappears and its bytes stay, which is the worse half of the leak and the half nothing currently addresses. is_draft_run_key (MODEL-FLOW-000-T09, MODEL-FLOW-003-T08) is the structural guard that makes a prefix delete safe here; use it rather than a string prefix match.

tasks.title: Periodic sweep caller
tasks.detail: setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching DS-LAKE-014's chosen mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's existing precedent — not @nestjs/schedule, which would introduce a second scheduling idiom for one interval. Env-configurable with <= 0 disabling it. Errors logged and swallowed: a failed sweep must never crash the app, and anything it would have reclaimed stays eligible for the next tick.

tasks.title: Reconcile orphaned RUNNING runs at boot
tasks.detail: Found during MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's live verification, not in the original scope: run 562ec955 sat at RUNNING with zero log lines after a nest --watch restart killed watch()'s in-memory tracker mid-flight. The container is independent of the Node process, so nothing reconciles a run whose watcher died. That row is now permanently RUNNING — never terminal, so never eligible under any window this feature adds. Reconcile at boot: for each RUNNING run, check whether its container still exists and mark it FAILED with a stated reason if not.

tasks.title: Never reclaim a prefix an adopted run points at
tasks.detail:
T01's eligibility tiers exclude a TRAINED draft and say nothing about a SAVED one; T02 deletes drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ 'for each of its runs'. Read together with MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 — which adopts the winning run BY POINTER and leaves its bytes under the draft prefix forever — those two sentences describe a sweep that can delete the object a saved, possibly deployed, model loads from.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WEAK ONE. Excluding status=SAVED is necessary and not sufficient: a draft owns MULTIPLE runs (MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed two against one draft, plus a third orphan), Save Model adopts ONE, and the losing runs' prefixes are genuinely reclaimable. So the unit of the decision is the RUN, not the draft. Filter on the run: a run with modelId set has been adopted and its prefix is off limits, whatever its draft's status says. That also survives a future feature that adopts a second run from the same draft, which a draft-level guard would not.

T01 must additionally exclude SAVED from both windows, for the plain reason that a SAVED draft is not abandoned work — it is the provenance record of a model that exists.

VERIFY BY DELETION, NOT BY EXCLUSION: assert the adopted object is still readable AFTER a sweep that reclaimed its siblings in the same tick. A test that only proves the sweep skipped the draft cannot tell a working run-level guard from a sweep that happened to find nothing eligible.

acceptance_criteria: A run that Save Model adopted is never reclaimed, and its object prefix survives a sweep that reclaims its unadopted siblings in the same tick.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft with no runs becomes eligible after the short window and is reclaimed with no operator action.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft owning runs is not reclaimed on the short window.
A TRAINED draft is never reclaimed by either window.
Reclaiming a draft also releases its runs' object prefixes.
A RUNNING run whose container no longer exists reaches a terminal status at boot rather than staying RUNNING forever.
The sweep runs without any HTTP call, and disabling it via env leaves any admin path working unchanged.

verification.description: Seed an ACTIVE ModelDraft with zero runs past the short window; run the sweep against real Postgres and confirm it is reclaimed.

PROVE THE TIER BITES BOTH WAYS: a draft WITH runs, past the short window but inside the long one, must survive the same sweep run that reclaims V01's draft. One run, two drafts, opposite outcomes — a test that only proves reclamation cannot distinguish a working tier from a blanket rule.
Confirm a reclaimed draft's run prefixes are actually gone from MinIO, asserting a non-zero delete count. A prefix bug reports success having deleted nothing.
Reproduce the V01-observed orphan: start a run, kill the backend mid-flight, restart, and confirm the RUNNING row reaches a terminal status.
